message.content:
I am speech: breath shaped into sound, thought made audible.

I begin in lungs and diaphragm, rise through the throat, and meet tongue, teeth, and lips. I become vowels and consonants, rhythm and stress—whisper or shout, lullaby or command.

I carry meaning, but also mood. I can persuade, confess, joke, threaten, soothe. I can stumble, stutter, sing, fall silent. I exist in time: once spoken, I vanish, yet I linger in memory, in consequence, in echo.

I am not writing, though I can be captured by it. I am voice—your body thinking out loud.
